notes.intake: Rule-based guess: line ID from the image name (table, matches 100% of images against genetic/knockouts_012.csv.gz::rows).
notes.images: Subject size shifts with the source image dimensions (about 1.24x between imaging setups): a magnification change, so each image-size group is scaled to the largest group. Brightness and contrast drift with imaging month and setup, so each image is stretched between its own subject percentiles. The grey-scale legend on 68% of images is painted over. Excluded 12: 7 inverted X-rays and 1 sideways view (subject darker than its background), and 2 pairs of identical pictures filed under different mice. The 374 grey-background images flagged for review are kept; normalisation evens them out.
notes.traits: Eight body and X-ray measurements that outline real structure. None tracks an imported IMPC trait: the high correlations with the caudal vertebra count rest on the few mice that have it, so every trait is scored against the same measurement on the real X-rays. Vertebra and rib counts and tibia length need a skeleton segmenter, which this recipe does not have.
notes.genetics: Each line differs at only a few columns (or there are few markers), so every column is read directly instead of through a PCA.
notes.training: large gives 4395 parameters per image against a target of 4200 for this image variety (42 PCs for 90%); 210 diffusion and 80 LiteVAE epochs match the earlier runs' steps.
notes.qc: Both runs finished cleanly. The LiteVAE's loss spikes were caught by the spike guard and it recovered within two epochs each time; its best checkpoint (epoch 74, validation loss 0.0015) is well after the last one. The diffusion model converged, uses the genotype about equally on held-out and training mice (gain 0.047 vs 0.050, so no memorisation), and its epoch-200 previews look like real X-rays and vary between seeds. Use the best diffusion checkpoint (epoch 207) for the analysis.

qc_issues: Diffusion (large) ran all 210 epochs; validation loss is flat at 0.0525 from about epoch 200 (best 0.05253 at epoch 207). The genotype gain is 0.047 on held-out mice and 0.050 on training mice, so the model uses the genotype about equally on unseen mice: no sign of memorisation.

LiteVAE training loss jumped at epochs 9, 23, 31, 40 and 59, and the spike guard skipped 142-360 steps in each. Only epoch 9 disturbed the weights (validation loss 28.5 for one epoch); validation was back to 0.0039 by epoch 11, and every later spike left validation loss unchanged. The best checkpoint, epoch 74 (validation 0.00149), comes long after the last spike.
copy: Images plus a genotype file. Here: 8,819 mouse X-rays as downloaded, nothing cleaned.
Code matches every image to its mouse and finds the genotypes, the sex and the imaging dates.
When the rules aren’t sure, an AI agent decides. It caught legends, a zoom change, inverted X-rays and duplicates.
And how to read the DNA: eight body measurements, every knockout column read directly.
It sizes the model and writes the job scripts. The models trained on the university cluster.
The agent read the loss curves, explained the spikes, ruled out memorisation and picked the checkpoint.
Every trait scored on 742 held-out mice against genomic prediction. From a folder to this, no code written.
